summary.text: Laurie Buckhout, a Republican and retired U.S. Army colonel, lost the November 3, 2026 election for North Carolina's redrawn 1st Congressional District to incumbent Don Davis, a rematch of the 2024 general election, which Davis won.
She founded and later sold a cyber and electronic warfare consulting business and served in the Pentagon's cyber policy office.

paragraphs.text: Laurie Buckhout was born in Virginia and lives in Edenton, North Carolina, with her husband Paul, a retired Army officer; they have two sons, according to her campaign website.

She earned a bachelor's degree from James Madison University, a master's of military arts and science in national military strategy, and a master's of science in information management from Webster University.

Buckhout was commissioned a second lieutenant in the Army Signal Corps in 1984 and served 26 years, retiring as a colonel in 2010; according to a candidate-supplied biography, she commanded a task force in the initial attack into Iraq in 2003.
After retiring from the Army, she founded Corvus Consulting, which specialized in electronic warfare and cyberspace operations; it was sold to Castellum Inc. in 2019, according to SIGNAL Media.
She served as Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Cyber Policy and was later named acting Assistant Secretary of War for cyber policy by President Trump.
Buckhout was the Republican nominee in 2024 and lost the general election to Davis.
She won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary over Carteret County Sheriff Asa Buck, 23,531 votes to 20,974.
During the campaign, she emphasized lowering costs, securing the border and strengthening national defense, and her campaign described her as a "constitutional conservative."
She received 46.8% of the vote to Don Davis's 50.1%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
